summary: Iter 9 — Stripe Connect (partner onboard/status) + customer receipt email on public coupon pay. 8/8 backend pytest passed. Frontend: partner-connect-card + partner-connect-status + partner-connect-button (click keeps user on /parceiro; informative Stripe/Connect message present). PublicCoupon /c/CLUB-10 with public-pay-email visible, amount 50 → redirects to checkout.stripe.com showing €45.00 (10% desconto), item 'Parceiro Exemplo · Campanha Exemplo · Cupom CLUB-10 · 10% de desconto aplicado sobre 50.00€' and Email field prefilled cliente.test@club.pt. Stripe 3DS not completable headlessly, so paid branch of fulfil() + public-receipt UI not fully E2E; verified via GET /api/payments/status/{sid} that pending returns kind=coupon_pay, gross_amount=50, discount=5, coupon=CLUB-10.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_payments.connect_onboard degrades gracefully to 200 {available:false} only when Stripe error text contains 'signed up for Connect'. Any other Stripe error becomes 502. That is acceptable but note that Stripe wording may change; consider matching account.create failure code as well.

routes_payments.fulfil coupon_pay branch calls send_email inside the transaction lifecycle and only sets receipt_emailed if email is provided. mailer.send_email should return False (not raise) when Resend is not configured — verified indirectly. Not tested E2E in this iteration.

GET /api/payments/status auto-fulfils from Stripe on demand — good UX for headless webhook environments, but be aware two concurrent status calls could race; the find_one_and_update guard in fulfil() prevents double-insert of redemption which is the important invariant.
Public /c/CLUB-10 exposes checkout email field with only client-side validation; backend also lowercases + strips. Fine.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of scripted flows (excluding real Stripe 3DS card entry)
